standard.title: Apply skills to enhance communication
standard.description: apply technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning (Y7-8, AC9ADA8C02). They have worked with strength, balance, coordination, and have used feedback to refine technical and expressive quality.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply technical and expressive skills and genre- or style-specific techniques to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Genre/style-specific technique application
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify characteristic techniques in a selected genre or style and apply them to enhance performance of dances in that style.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least three characteristic techniques of a selected genre/style and demonstrating them in performance — with attention to safe execution.
nodes.typical_width: Using observations/analysis of a dance in a selected genre/style to identify characteristic techniques; building ability to execute techniques using safe dance practice over time; applying techniques to enhance performance; seeking feedback on choreography and performance using Viewpoints questions.
wider: Study a genre or style from a culture students identify with — using cultural knowledge to inform authentic technique application rather than imitation
Compare how the same technique functions differently in two related genres/styles — developing nuanced style-literacy

response_modes.reason: Style-specific technique develops through sustained engagement with the genre's movement vocabulary. Identify the characteristic techniques explicitly, then build repetition across sessions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop technique in multiple genre/style contexts build stylistic range and can make informed choices about which technical vocabulary serves a specific communicative purpose.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least three characteristic techniques of their selected genre/style
Student demonstrates these techniques in performance with safe execution

nodes.label: Applying musculoskeletal knowledge to safe technique
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply knowledge of the musculoskeletal system to execute movement techniques safely and prevent injury.
nodes.minimum_width: Explaining at least one musculoskeletal principle relevant to a technique they are practising; applying it to modify or refine execution.
nodes.typical_width: Applying knowledge of the structure and function of the musculoskeletal system to execute movements safely; preventing injury to self and others; connecting anatomical understanding to technique decisions in a specific genre/style.
wider: Analyse a physically demanding technique in their chosen style through an anatomical lens — identifying injury risks and safe practice modifications
Research how professional dance practitioners in their chosen style approach injury prevention and recovery — applying this knowledge to their own practice
nodes.hinge_reason: At Y9-10, technical demands increase significantly and students work with genre-specific technique that carries real injury risk if executed without anatomical awareness. Students who lack this knowledge cannot safely pursue the level of technical challenge expected.

response_modes.reason: Anatomical knowledge requires explicit instruction — it does not arise naturally from movement practice alone. Teach relevant musculoskeletal concepts in direct connection to the techniques being practised, not as standalone science content.

success_criteria: Student can explain how at least one musculoskeletal principle applies to the safe execution of a specific technique
Student consistently applies safe practice principles when executing demanding techniques

nodes.label: Seeking feedback and refining
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can seek and use feedback on choreography and performance to refine technical and expressive skill application.
nodes.minimum_width: Seeking feedback on at least one aspect of performance using a Viewpoints question; making at least one identifiable refinement in response.
nodes.typical_width: Seeking feedback on choreography and performance using Viewpoints questions ('What emotion did you feel most strongly?'); using feedback to refine technical and expressive skills; evaluating the success of skill application in communicating intent.
wider: Seek feedback from multiple sources (peer, teacher, video self-review) on the same performance — synthesising across feedback sources to prioritise development areas
Document a feedback-revision cycle — recording the feedback received, the decision made in response, and the effect on the work

response_modes.reason: Using feedback to refine integrates technical skill, expressive skill, and reflective capacity. Frame feedback-seeking as a professional practice — dancers in all genres use this cycle throughout their careers.

success_criteria: Student seeks specific feedback on performance using at least one Viewpoints question
Student makes an identifiable refinement to technical or expressive skill application in response to feedback received
